title: Understanding PVC vs. ABS for Drainage Systems
description: Both Schedule 40 PVC and ABS are widely used non-metallic piping materials for residential drain, waste, and vent (DWV) installations. ABS is a black plastic pipe valued for its high impact strength and straightforward single-step solvent welding process. White Schedule 40 PVC offers excellent chemical resistance and rigidity, but demands a two-step installation using primer followed by solvent cement. Selection typically depends on regional building codes, temperature variations, and material availability. Standard solvent cements cannot bond PVC to ABS directly, so plumbers must use approved mechanical couplings or specialized transition solvent where local codes permit.

Understanding PVC vs. ABS for Drainage Systems

Both Schedule 40 PVC and ABS are widely used non-metallic piping materials for residential drain, waste, and vent (DWV) installations. ABS is a black plastic pipe valued for its high impact strength and straightforward single-step solvent welding process. White Schedule 40 PVC offers excellent chemical resistance and rigidity, but demands a two-step installation using primer followed by solvent cement. Selection typically depends on regional building codes, temperature variations, and material availability. Standard solvent cements cannot bond PVC to ABS directly, so plumbers must use approved mechanical couplings or specialized transition solvent where local codes permit.
